title: His father and Johnny Wiggs at school; Irvin Leclere and Triangle Jazz Blues
summary: His father and Johnny Wiggs were schoolmates; Steinau also recounts learning in San Francisco that Irvin Leclere lived near his childhood home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: But, uh, I think it's interesting that your father and Johnny went to, uh...
High school. They went to high school? Yeah, they went to Warren Eastern. I see. It must have been Warren Eastern.
That must have been the only Boys High.

I think it was, and I think it may have been known as Boys High at that time. I don't think it was Warren Eastern to start off with. No, Johnny, it was a strange thing. At least I took it as strange. Uh, because there were people around doing stuff in music and in jazz, within pretty close radius. But my father, back, I guess around 19, the late 40s or around 1950, when I met Johnny Wiggs and liked him, uh, and I don't remember who said it, I think it was my father who said so, uh, said something, oh, is that Johnny Hyman? Uh-huh. And I said, yeah, I think so. And they had been in high school together and apparently had been good friends. And my father's impression of it was that Johnny always got him into trouble. Mm-hmm. Which, of course, may or may not have been so, considering this was 30 years or so later, 30 or 35 years later than the actual happenings involved. But they had been in school together and had liked each other and certainly remembered each other, although neither of them spoke much in detail except that, uh, that they had gotten into mischief together from time to time. Yeah, I don't think Johnny ever told me about that. And I don't think when he met you that your name probably didn't register. I don't think so. I know there was another thing, a similar sort of thing. In 19, uh, when I was an intern in San Francisco in 1952-53, uh, Turek Murphy's band was playing a tune called Triangle Jazz Blues, which, uh, Turek talked about having accidentally run across by Irvin Leclair and, uh, said nobody had ever heard of him or had ever heard of the tune before, let alone, uh, there having been a recording made. And somehow, I don't remember how, it might have been you who told me, Leclair had lived and I think may still have been living, uh, two blocks from where I, where I grew up. He lived just on the other side of Claiborne Avenue. Yeah.
